newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady, demand grows.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady, demand grows.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady on Friday in spite of dwindling offers and growing demand as most banks were due to pay their weekly taxes, dealers said.
"Banks announced more spending because of tax payments for the current week, but supply was still sufficient to cover their needs," one dealer said.
Midmorning trade (by 0900 GMT) totalled 56.3 million kuna. Of this 43 million was call money borrowed at a stable 8.0 percent rate with a few smaller transactions at 7.0 percent.
Bankers also charged 7.0 percent for fresh four-day loans.
Insurers lent one-month funds at 11 percent, while savings banks payed 16 and 18 percent for the same period.
Overnight trade on Thursday consisted of a single 3.7 million deal as all other banks were liquid with overall balances totalling 757 million kuna.
The central bank said Lombard borrowings shrank further to 2.5 million from 6.2 million on Thursday. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
